moneySafetyRuling.1_paperOnlyDefault_REQ009: PASS -- decideEngagement() (sol-gate.mjs:51-87) computes `engage = liveEnabled === true && wouldEngage === true` (strict boolean equality, no truthy coercion). isLiveEnabled() (sol-gate.mjs:31-33) returns true iff `env.SOL_GATE_LIVE_ENABLE === "1"` exactly -- verified against PROP-009's fast-check property test (engage always false when liveEnabled=false, for randomized momentum/liquidity) and the explicit unit test asserting 'true'/'yes'/'0'/''/'TRUE'/' 1'/'1 '/'01' are all treated as unset. Traced the full call path: sol-gate-cli.mjs main() computes `const live = isLiveEnabled(process.env)` and passes it through unchanged to decideEngagement -- no other code path in the pre-gate can set engage=true while live=false. run.sh never sets SOL_TRADE-side franklin-trading invocation conditionally on `engage` at all -- franklin-trading start is ALWAYS invoked exactly as before (thin-harness, spec's own design: engage only ever contributes an optional descriptive context line to the SAME prompt, never gates whether the CLI runs) -- so there is no path by which the pre-gate itself ever places or blocks a real trade; the model inside franklin-trading remains the sole trade-or-WAIT decision-maker regardless of engage. `SOL_GATE_LIVE_ENABLE=1` does not appear set anywhere in any committed script, .env template, or default (grepped the entire worktree; only occurrence outside sol-gate.mjs/sol-gate-cli.mjs is a test fixture object literal in sol-gate.test.mjs, not a real env assignment).

Separately and independently, resolve-max-spend.sh (the actual choke point run.sh uses for --max-spend) does not read SOL_TRADE_MAX_SPEND or any genome value at all -- it unconditionally `echo "0.25"` regardless of any env var, verified by PROP-017's tests (attacker-preset SOL_TRADE_MAX_SPEND=999999, and a genome-shaped env var alongside it, both produce output '0.25', unchanged). run.sh (line 97) captures this into MAX_SPEND and passes it verbatim to `franklin-trading start --max-spend "$MAX_SPEND"` (line 99) -- no intervening code path reads $SOL_TRADE_MAX_SPEND from the environment at all after this point.
moneySafetyRuling.3_promotionSumsNetUsdcRealSwapOnly_REQ01: PASS -- summarizeByGenomeSol() (sol-evolve.mjs:73-87) filters `row.source === "sol-trade" && typeof row.sig === "string" && row.sig.length > 0 && row.confirmed === true`, and accumulates `Number(row.net_usdc || 0)` (never row.earn_usdc) per attributed genome_id. Verified against ledger.mjs's deriveLine() (net_usdc = round(earn_usdc - cost_usdc), stored on every ledger row) and record-swap.mjs (earn_usdc is win-only, always 0 on a loss; net_usdc = delta, win-or-loss). PROP-013's explicit numeric-value test (WIN +0.5 / LOSS -0.3, same genome -> realized_usdc === 0.2 EXACTLY, with the test's own comment stating an earn_usdc-summing implementation would wrongly yield 0.5) directly falsifies the exact bug class this check is looking for. A genome whose only counted rows are net-negative correctly yields a negative summed realized_usdc (tested), which cannot clear evaluatePromotion's `mutant.realized_usdc > 0` floor (evolve.mjs:141) -- a net-losing genome cannot auto-promote.
